minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved the 12 Kimble Street sewer extension; chairman John Reynolds announced he will resign at end of August.
minutes.summary: The commission approved a sewer extension plan for 12 Kimble Street with a condition to pave the full disturbed length of road. Most of the meeting covered Q4 billing and demand problems, the MUNIS software outages, ARPA funding requests, and a newspaper ad about flushing items that clog pump stations. The chairman announced he is stepping down at the end of August.

votes.motion: Accept the 12 Kimble Street sewer extension plan with the condition that the entire disturbed length of street be paved curb to curb
Approve the FY24 sewer commitments pending the final total
Sewer department to pay for a full page color newspaper ad about clogs

budget_items.topic: Q4 FY24 sewer billing and demands
budget_items.what_was_said: Demand notices were delayed and sent with relabelled due dates; the fiscal year had not closed so budget-to-revenue status could not be given.
The town has remaining ARPA money and departments were asked to submit requests by July 31st. The commission discussed requesting recovery of lost demand revenue and consultant costs.

budget_items.topic: Lost demand revenue and MUNIS consultant fee
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager estimated lost demand (interest) revenue and noted the consultant's daily rate, which she felt the commission should not pay.

budget_items.topic: Mass One pump station suction line repair
budget_items.what_was_said: The earlier Mass One repair cost was recalled and the new repair would probably cost more due to excavation; an estimate was requested for the ARPA submission.
Half page and full page ad costs were stated, and the commission voted to pay for a full page color ad.
The consultant recommended an on-premises service contract with a cost; commissioners said the town should fund it since the server issue affects all of town hall.
The earlier grant was not awarded for lack of sufficient energy savings; the town hopes to bundle a pump station upgrade into an October proposal.

decisions.decision: The commission will submit three ARPA requests: lost demand revenue, consultant fees, and the Mass One suction line work; Bill Bernard to prepare the Mass One estimate by July 31.
Minutes from the last two meetings will be voted on at the next meeting because they were not on the agenda.
The ad will carry a message from the Lunenburg Sewer Commission at the top, with 'toilet paper only' bolded and a count of 31 clogs in 10 months.
Commissioners to review the manhole inspection IFB and send comments individually to the chair and Bill Bernard.

what_happened.line: The commission approved a 12 Kimble Street sewer extension plan, with a condition to pave the full disturbed length of road, though the count was only partly audible.
The commission decided to submit three ARPA requests: lost demand revenue, consultant fees, and repair of the Mass One suction line.
It approved the FY24 sewer commitments pending the final total, and voted to pay for a full page color newspaper ad about flushing items that clog pump stations.
Q4 FY24 demand notices were delayed and sent with relabelled due dates, so budget-to-revenue status could not be given because the fiscal year had not closed.
The chairman announced he will resign at the end of August.

why_it_matters: The ARPA requests and the Tyler Tech server contract bear on who pays for the town's software outages and lost sewer billing revenue, which touches the sewer budget and the rates behind sewer bills.
A new sewer extension and an ad aimed at pump-station clogs affect who connects to the system and what upkeep the sewer fund carries.
watch_next: Minutes from the last two meetings are to be voted on at the next meeting, since they were not on the agenda.
The Mass One suction line estimate for the ARPA submission was due July 31, and the ARPA requests were due that day.
